Import Wildcards

Resolver .json, or Dynamic Prompts .txt and .yaml (or a .zip of a wildcards folder).

Tick: import or skip. Tap a name to see what's in it.

How To

Type these into a wildcard's options (one per line) or straight into a prompt. They work in Basic too. TRY shows what gets picked and why.

Pick one of a few

Put the choices in curly brackets, split by |. One is picked each image, without needing a wildcard of its own.

{red|blue|green} dress→blue dress

Sometimes nothing

Leave one choice empty. Two choices, one empty, gives it half the time; {glasses||} a third.

{glasses|}→glasses, half the time

Pick several

A number and $$ first picks that many different ones. {1-3$$…} picks one to three. Works with a wildcard too: {2$$__props__}.

{2$$hat|scarf|gloves}→hat, gloves

More or less likely

A number and :: at the start of an option sets how often it's picked compared with the others (1 when there's none). Only at the start of a line; anywhere else it's sent as text.

3::red hair→3× as likely
0.5::bald→half as likely

Use the same pick again

Give a pick a name with ${name=!…}. It shows nothing there; ${name} then puts the same pick anywhere in the prompt, negative or Hi-Res, so two places always match.

${hair=!__hair color__}→picks once
${hair}→that same pick

Label options

Words after ## are labels for the options below to work with. They're never sent to the image. A line of just labels gives them to every option in the wildcard.

library ## indoor, quiet
## pose→every option labeled pose

Only some options

Labels in square brackets after the name: only options with those labels can be picked. & means and, | or, ! not.

__places[indoor]__→library or cafe, never beach
__places[indoor & !busy]__

Only if…

Start an option with ?label:: and it can only be picked when something with that label is in the image, wherever it's written in the prompt. ?!label:: means only when it isn't.

?sitting:: relaxed→only with a sitting pose

Never together

A line starting #! is a rule for the whole image. It starts counting once its wildcard is used.

#! sitting excludes standing→never both
#! one of: hat, hood→at most one
#! wet requires rain→wet only with rain

Set a theme for the whole image

A wildcard of named picks, labels and rules, anywhere in the prompt. Everything else follows: winter date holding the lines below makes options labeled swimwear impossible.

${season=!winter} ## winter
#! excludes swimwear
__winter date__, __outfit__→no swimwear

Random LoRA or style

Picks a different one for each image. LoRAs come from the ones given that type in their settings, for this tab's model.

random::character→a Character LoRA
random::style→one of your styles

Putting it together

Places are labeled, the pose labels what it is, and the mood follows the pose, in any order.

places: library ## indoor / beach ## outdoor
pose: sitting ## sitting / standing
mood: ?sitting:: relaxed / alert
prompt: __places[indoor]__, __pose__, __mood__

CHECK finds missing names, loops and rules that clash.

Color-Coded Prompts

Colors the text in every prompt and negative box so a missing or extra bracket stands out. Nothing changes in what is sent.

(((Brackets, a color for each level of nesting )A bracket with no partner :1.2 3::Weights (3:: weights an option in a wildcard) <lora:x>LoRA tags __x__Wildcards {a|b}Choices BREAKBREAK and AND ?!a::Conditions (in wildcards) #! excludesRules (in wildcards) ## labelLabels (in wildcards; not sent) # noteComments (in wildcards) [tag:0.5]Check this: Forge reads it as "add after 50%", not a weight

Prompt Guide

Formatting you can use in any prompt or negative box.

Order matters

Tags are split by commas; earlier ones count a little more.

1girl, red dress, beach→dress and beach a touch weaker than 1girl

Stronger

Round brackets: 1.1× per pair, or set a number (0.5 to 1.5 works best).

(smile)→1.1×
((smile))→1.21×
(smile:1.3)→1.3×

Weaker

Square brackets: 0.9×. Or a number below 1 in round brackets.

[freckles]→0.9×
(freckles:0.7)→0.7×

Brackets as text

A backslash keeps a bracket as text, as in series names.

rem \(re:zero\)→the tag "rem (re:zero)"

Swap partway

The first tag until that point, then the second. Below 1 is a share of the steps; 1 or more is a step number.

[cat:dog:0.5]→cat for the first half, then dog
[cat:dog:10]→dog takes over after step 10

Add or remove later

One colon adds the tag from that point; two colons remove it. Not a weight.

[hat:0.5]→a hat added halfway
[hat:12]→a hat added after step 12
[hat::12]→the hat taken away after step 12

Alternate

Square brackets split by | swap every step, blending the two.

[cat|dog]→a cat-dog mix

BREAK

Starts a new chunk of the prompt, so colors and details bleed less between parts.

red dress BREAK blue hat→the colors stay on their own items

AND

Separate prompts blended together, so each part keeps more to itself. Slower. SD 1.5 / SDXL only; for placing things, use Forge Couple.

a cat AND a dog→less mixing of the two
a cat :1.2 AND a dog :0.8→more cat than dog

LoRA

Put its trigger words in the prompt too. Two character LoRAs: about 0.6 each.

<lora:name:0.8>→that LoRA at 0.8

Wildcards and choices

One option picked for each image. More in Wildcards > How To.

__hair color__→one of its options
{red|blue} dress→red or blue

In the negative

~word keeps tags ending in it out of the picks and out of the prompt.

~hat→no hat, sun hat or top hat
